top_stories.title: VMware vCenter zero-day exploited for months before patch (CVE-2026-123890)
top_stories.summary: A China-nexus espionage group exploited a VMware vCenter zero-day vulnerability (CVE-2026-123890, CVSS 9.8) for over two months before Broadcom released a patch. The flaw allows a remote, unauthenticated attacker to obtain an administrator session on vCenter Server, directly impacting privileged access and authentication controls.

top_stories.title: AI agent API security hasn’t caught up with agents already running in production
top_stories.summary: A Postman survey of nearly 9,000 developers, architects, and executives found that 25% of organizations already have AI agents calling APIs in production. Approximately 40% of respondents have not yet resolved how credentials and identity management will work for these agents.

top_stories.title: China-Linked Hackers Exploit Critical VMware vCenter Zero-Day to Gain Admin Access and Steal Data
top_stories.summary: A China-linked threat group known as Armory Castle exploited a critical zero-day vulnerability (CVE-2026-123890, CVSS 9.8) in VMware vCenter Server in early September 2026. The flaw is an authentication bypass in the VMware Directory Service that allowed attackers to gain unauthorized admin access and steal data.

top_stories.title: New Attack Bypasses TPM Lockout to Crack Windows Hello and BitLocker PINs in Days, Not Years
top_stories.summary: Researchers at Technische Universität Berlin discovered an attack that bypasses TPM lockout mechanisms on AMD-based and some Intel PCs, allowing brute-force cracking of Windows Hello and BitLocker PINs within days. By physically opening a device and resetting the TPM lockout counter, attackers were able to recover a four-digit Windows Hello PIN and a six-digit BitLocker PIN in lab testing.

top_stories.title: Java4Shell Flaw (CVE-2026-114938) Enables Pre-Auth RCE in Jira, Jenkins, Keycloak and More
top_stories.summary: A pre-authentication remote code execution vulnerability dubbed Java4Shell (CVE-2026-114938) has been disclosed by security firm Calif, affecting Java 17.0.6 and later on specific x86-64 processors. The flaw impacts several widely used platforms including Keycloak, an open-source identity and access management solution, as well as Jira and Jenkins.

news.title: Still tracking company passwords in spreadsheets? You’re flying blind.
news.summary: NordPass published content advocating for centralized password management over spreadsheet-based credential tracking for IT administrators. The piece covers credential visibility, identifying weak or reused passwords, and secure sharing practices.

news.title: Windows 11 KB5132057 update released with 28 changes and fixes
news.summary: Microsoft released the KB5132057 preview update for Windows 11, which includes 28 changes and fixes. Among the updates are improvements to Windows Hello, the biometric authentication feature built into Windows 11.

news.title: authentik version/2026.8.6
news.summary: authentik released version 2026.8.6 of its open-source identity provider platform. The release supports SAML, OAuth2/OIDC, LDAP, and RADIUS protocols for centralized authentication, authorization, and access management.

news.title: Anzeige: Microsoft Entra ID: Identitäten und Zugriffe sicher verwalten
news.summary: Microsoft Entra ID is featured in a sponsored advertisement promoting identity and access management capabilities. The ad highlights a workshop covering hybrid environment configuration and security strategies using the platform.

news.title: Critical VMware vCenter Zero-Day Flaw Lets Network Attackers Bypass Authentication
news.summary: Broadcom disclosed a critical zero-day vulnerability in VMware vCenter that allows network-adjacent attackers to bypass authentication and gain unauthorized system access. Fixed versions have been released for all supported branches, with no available workaround for the authentication bypass flaw.

news.title: Your AWS Security, Identity, and Governance guide to re:Invent 2026
news.summary: AWS is previewing its Security, Identity, and Governance track for re:Invent 2026, scheduled for November 30 to December 4 in Las Vegas. The event will focus on identity challenges introduced by AI agents operating autonomously across systems, among other IAM-related topics.

news.title: IAM Roles Anywhere now supports aliases to simplify workload configuration
news.summary: AWS IAM Roles Anywhere has added support for aliases, allowing administrators to assign human-readable names to trust anchors, profiles, and certificate revocation lists (CRLs). Workloads can now request temporary credentials using these alias names instead of ARNs, simplifying configuration and management.

news.title: Amazon Cognito now supports AWS Secrets Manager for app client secrets
news.summary: Amazon Cognito has added integration with AWS Secrets Manager, enabling user pool app client secrets to be stored and managed through Secrets Manager. This update affects how developers secure authentication credentials for applications built on Cognito's sign-in and access control platform.

news.title: Identity context is essential for exposure management: Tenable One adds ways to bring in identity security data
news.summary: Tenable One has added the ability to ingest identity findings from third-party sources within its exposure management platform. The new capability allows security teams to assess and prioritize identity-related exposures such as stale and overprivileged accounts alongside vulnerability and misconfiguration data.

news.title: Bitwarden expands passkey support with new Windows and macOS integrations
news.summary: Bitwarden has expanded passkey support with new integrations for Windows and macOS, enabling users to log in and unlock their vaults using passkeys through native OS authentication. The update extends passkey functionality across both desktop platforms, aligning with broader FIDO2/passwordless authentication standards relevant to IAM practitioners.

news.title: Major Brazilian Signature Apps Enable RCE & Fraud
news.summary: Brazilian government-sanctioned authentication middleware used for legally binding document signing contains remote code execution vulnerabilities. The flaws affect signature applications that serve as authentication mechanisms for high-stakes legal documents in Brazil.

news.title: Step-up authentication: how to right-size authentication to risk
news.summary: The article covers step-up authentication, a risk-based approach that requires additional identity verification only when users attempt higher-risk actions within an application. It explains how authentication requirements can be calibrated to the sensitivity of specific actions, such as distinguishing between viewing account data versus initiating financial transactions.

news.title: Detecting cross-cloud lateral movement with AWS Security Hub
news.summary: The article addresses detecting cross-cloud lateral movement by attackers who compromise identities and follow federated trusts across cloud providers. It focuses on using AWS Security Hub to identify this identity-based attack pattern in multicloud environments.

news.title: NIST Finalizes Post-Quantum Cryptography Guidance, GAO Offers a Reality Check
news.summary: NIST has finalized its post-quantum cryptography guidance as GAO released a report showing federal agencies are behind in implementing quantum-resistant defenses. Post-quantum cryptography directly impacts IAM systems that rely on encryption for authentication, key exchange, and secure identity protocols.

news.title: Extortion Group Luna Moth Flits Into Law Firms a Second Time
news.summary: The Luna Moth extortion group is targeting law firms using social engineering tactics designed to steal Microsoft access tokens. The campaign involves retargeting organizations that previously refused to pay ransoms, with credential and token theft as the primary attack vector.

news.title: Microsoft Fixes Nearly 1,100 Security Vulnerabilities
news.summary: Microsoft released a Patch Tuesday update addressing nearly 1,100 security vulnerabilities, including 63 critical flaws. Among the fixes is a zero-day vulnerability in Microsoft Outlook, alongside updates from other software vendors including Adobe, Apple, Google, and Mozilla.
